lessons.plainEnglish: The point scale sorts violations into four bands. Eight points is reserved for one offense only: fleeing from an officer. Six points covers the four worst remaining offenses - speeding in a school zone, reckless driving, hit and run, and speeding 20 mph or more over the limit. Three points covers the everyday failures at intersections and in traffic: running a light or a stop sign, failing to yield, an illegal pass, driving left of center, driving the wrong way on a one way street. Two points is the floor, and covers handling errors such as improper backing, improper turning and following too closely - and anything the table does not name at all.
lessons.whyItMatters: Points are the arithmetic behind losing your licence. Six points brings a letter of caution, and twelve points makes your licence subject to suspension. In those terms, one fleeing conviction is two thirds of the way to suspension, two six-point offenses reach it exactly, and four three-point convictions do the same. Speeding shows the logic most clearly: the further over the limit you are caught, the higher the band, which is why 19 mph over costs 5 points and 20 mph over costs 6.
lessons.example: You are caught 22 mph over the limit: that is the top speeding band, 6 points. A few months later you are convicted of failure to obey a traffic light: 3 points. You then get an improper signal ticket: 2 points. You are at 11 points - one 2-point conviction away from having your licence subject to suspension.

lessons.plainEnglish: Every yellow diamond names one hazard and, usually, one action. A curve is too sharp for normal highway speed, so slow before it. A crossroads means vehicles may pull out, so look. A lane ends, so merge early - and check which side the symbol points to, because it reverses for a left-lane ending. Merging traffic will come into your lane, so adjust speed or move over. A hill needs speed shed before the descent starts. A slippery section needs less speed while it is wet. A low clearance shows a height you must compare with your own vehicle. A pedestrian crossing needs you watching and ready to yield.
lessons.whyItMatters: Warning signs are the only traffic control device that gives you time. A stop sign tells you what to do at the moment you arrive; a warning diamond tells you what is coming while you still have distance to work with. Nearly every one of these signs has a built-in instruction - slow down, watch, be ready, yield - and the test asks for that instruction as often as it asks for the hazard.
lessons.example: You crest a rise on a two-lane highway and see a yellow diamond with a curving arrow and a black-on-yellow '35' below it. The 35 is not the legal limit for the road - it is the advisory speed for that curve. You slow to it before the curve begins, not while you are already turning.

lessons.plainEnglish: Four of these signs forbid something. No U-Turn bans turning around mid-street or at the intersection. No Right Turn and No Left Turn each ban one direction, usually because the turn would put you onto a one way street the wrong way. Wrong Way and Do Not Enter both say the same thing: traffic that way is prohibited. The rest assign lanes. A One Way sign describes the cross street, not yours. A Dual Turn Lane sign marks the centre lane that left-turning drivers from both directions share - which is also why you must never pass in it. Lane Directions signs sit at the gaps in a divider and remind you which side you belong on.
lessons.whyItMatters: These are the signs that stop a driver from ending up head-on in traffic. The handbook is blunt about it: take a lane marked Wrong Way or Do Not Enter and you will likely run into another vehicle. And the consequence is on the record as well as on the road - driving the wrong way on a one way street is a 3-point conviction on the point scale.
lessons.example: You want to turn left, but the cross street carries a One Way sign with traffic coming toward you, and a No Left Turn sign hangs above the intersection. The two signs are telling you the same thing from different angles: that turn would put you into oncoming traffic. Because consecutive one-way blocks usually run in opposite directions, the next street along is normally the one going your way.

lessons.plainEnglish: These signals hang directly above individual lanes, and each one governs only the lane beneath it. A green downward arrow means that lane is yours to use. A yellow X is a warning that the lane is about to be closed or about to reverse direction, and you should move out of it as soon as you safely can. A red X means the lane is already closed, or is now carrying traffic in the opposite direction - do not use it at all.
lessons.whyItMatters: On a reversible lane the danger is not a fine, it is a head-on collision. A lane that carried you inbound this morning can be carrying vehicles the other way this evening, and the only thing telling you which is true right now is the signal above your head. The colours follow the same grammar as a traffic light: green permits, yellow warns of a change coming, red prohibits.
lessons.example: You are commuting home in the inside lane when the green arrow above it switches to a yellow X. That is your notice that the lane is about to reverse for the opposite rush. choices: Stay in your lane, because a turning lane must never be used to overtake and pass
Use the turning lane briefly to get past
Use it only if nobody is currently turning
Use it as long as you signal first
questions.explanation: The rule does not bend for convenience: never use a turning lane to overtake and pass. Traffic from either direction uses that lane, so a driver you cannot see may pull into it head-on while you are passing.
choiceExplanations: A brief pass in a turning lane is precisely what the handbook prohibits.
Traffic from either direction may enter the lane at any moment to turn.
Signalling does not turn a prohibited manoeuvre into a permitted one.

questions.question: What are Lane Directions signs there to remind you?
choices: Which side of the divider you belong on
How far it is to the next exit
What the speed limit is
Which lane is ending ahead
questions.explanation: The handbook says these signs are there to remind you which side of the divider you belong on. They are placed at the gaps in a divider, exactly where a driver could mistakenly turn into the wrong carriageway.
choiceExplanations: Distances to places and exits are given on green guide signs.
Speed limits are posted on their own white regulatory signs.
A lane ending is announced by a yellow diamond warning sign.

questions.question: Where does the handbook say Lane Directions signs are placed?
choices: Between divided highway lanes, at openings in the dividers where streets intersect the highway
On the shoulder of every interstate ramp
Above every signalised intersection
At the entrance to every school zone
questions.explanation: They are posted between the divided lanes of a highway and placed at the openings in the dividers where streets intersect. Those openings are the only points where a driver could enter the wrong side, which is why the reminder sits there.
choiceExplanations: Interstate ramps carry advisory speed and guide signs, not lane direction signs.
Signalised intersections are controlled by the signals themselves.
School zones are marked by five-sided school signs.

questions.question: Lane use control signals are installed for what situation?
choices: Where the direction of a street or a certain lane changes during the day
Where a signal has gone out of order
Where a work zone has been set up
Where a school zone is in force
questions.explanation: The handbook describes these as special signals used to control traffic when the direction of a street or certain lane changes during the day. They are what makes a reversible commuter lane possible.
choiceExplanations: An out-of-order signal is placed in flashing operation and treated as an intersection flasher.
Work zones are controlled by orange signs, barricades, drums, cones and flaggers.
School zones are controlled by speed limits and five-sided school signs.

questions.question: Which kind of signal tells you how a specific lane may be used at that moment?
choices: A lane use control signal
A crosswalk signal
An intersection flasher
An advisory speed sign
questions.explanation: Lane use control signals hang over individual lanes and indicate how those lanes may be used right now. That is different from an ordinary traffic light, which governs the whole approach rather than one lane's direction.
choiceExplanations: Crosswalk signals are traffic signals for pedestrians, not for lane assignment.
Intersection flashers supplement or replace stop signs; they do not assign lanes.
An advisory speed sign recommends a safe speed and does not control lane use.

questions.question: A red X is displayed over the lane you are driving in. What does it mean?
choices: The lane is closed or being used by opposing traffic, so do not use it
The lane is about to close, so move out when you can
You may use the lane beneath the signal
You must stop in the lane and wait
questions.explanation: A red X means the lane is closed or being used by opposing traffic, and the handbook's instruction is simply: do not use this lane. On a reversible road the lane under a red X may be carrying vehicles straight at you.
choiceExplanations: That description is the yellow X, which warns the lane is about to close or reverse.
Permission to use a lane is given by a green downward arrow, not a red X.
Stopping in a lane that may carry opposing traffic leaves you in its path.

questions.question: You are driving in a reversible lane and a red X appears above it. What must you do?
choices: Leave the lane, because it is closed or carrying opposing traffic
Continue, because the signal is for oncoming drivers
Slow to 15 mph and continue in the lane
Stop and wait in the lane for a green arrow
questions.explanation: The red X applies to the drivers beneath it, and it means the lane is closed or in use by opposing traffic. Clearing the lane is the only safe response, because the vehicles now entitled to that lane are coming the other way.
choiceExplanations: A lane use signal governs the lane it hangs over, which includes your lane.
No speed makes a lane carrying opposing traffic safe to occupy.
Waiting in a closed lane leaves you sitting in the path of opposing traffic.

questions.question: A yellow X appears over your lane. What is it telling you?
choices: The lane is about to be closed or reverse direction, so move out as soon as you can
The lane is already closed to all traffic
You may continue using the lane indefinitely
All traffic in the lane must stop
questions.explanation: A yellow X is a warning of a change: the lane is about to be closed, or its direction is about to reverse. The handbook tells you to move out of it as soon as you can, while there is still a gap to move into.
choiceExplanations: A lane that is already closed is marked with a red X.
The yellow X exists precisely to warn that the lane's status is about to change.
The yellow X asks you to move out of the lane, not to stop in it.

questions.question: What is the difference between a yellow X and a red X over a lane?
choices: The yellow X warns the lane is about to close or reverse; the red X means it is closed now
The yellow X means the lane is closed; the red X means it is about to close
They mean exactly the same thing
The yellow X applies to trucks and the red X to cars
questions.explanation: Yellow warns, red prohibits - the same logic as a traffic light. The yellow X gives you time to change lanes before the closure or reversal takes effect; by the time the red X shows, the lane may already be carrying opposing traffic.
choiceExplanations: That reverses the two: red is the closure and yellow is the advance warning.
They differ: one warns of a coming change, the other states a present closure.
Lane use control signals apply to all traffic in the lane, not to particular vehicle types.

You must turn at the next intersection
The lane is reserved for opposing traffic
questions.explanation: A green downward arrow means traffic may use the lane under the arrow. The arrow points down at the lane it refers to, which is how you tell which lane each signal is governing.
choiceExplanations: A lane about to close is shown by a yellow X.
The arrow points down at the lane below it; it is not a turn instruction.
A lane being used by opposing traffic is marked with a red X.

A red X

questions.explanation: Only the green downward arrow gives permission; the two X indications either warn of a change or prohibit use. Reading the signal above your own lane, rather than the one beside it, is the habit to build.
choiceExplanations: A yellow X warns that the lane is about to be closed or reversed.
A red X means the lane is closed or being used by opposing traffic.
A circular flashing yellow is an intersection flasher, not a lane use signal.

Only on interstate highways
Only on rural roads
Only where a traffic signal is present
questions.explanation: The handbook names intersections and school zones as the places to be aware of crosswalks, because they indicate somewhere with heavy pedestrian activity. Being especially alert in those places reduces the risk of crashes.

They are places where pedestrians must yield to all vehicles
They are always controlled by a traffic signal
They mark the boundary of a construction zone
